protections: P1: a setting value, including the trust decision input, is taken from the caller's own options entry for that key, with the schema default used only when the option is absent or explicitly undefined (src/Settings.ts:336-348, src/Settings.ts:328-334).

P2: isTrusted supplies a protocol derived from the context URL whenever the context does not already carry one, so a caller's trust function is handed a protocol KaTeX computed (src/Settings.ts:464-476, src/utils.ts:69-89).
P3: macro names resolve only from own properties of the per-render macro map and of the builtin macro map (src/Namespace.ts:68-71, src/Namespace.ts:81-87, src/Namespace.ts:96-122).
P4: CLI flag name, description, processor and default are taken from the schema entry that describes that flag (cli.js:26-31).
P5: auto-render resolves its render options locally before calling katex.render (contrib/auto-render/auto-render.ts:130-161).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: SETTINGS_SCHEMA is a module constant written in this same file, not caller input, so its entries are assumed not to be attacker-shaped; schema.default is present on only some entries and schema.processor on only three numeric ones, so both reads look like static bookkeeping rather than a decision path.

isTrusted is the check itself: it already derives the protocol and looks correct, and the reported shape is a polluted settings value, not a polluted context object, so there is nothing here a solver expects to change.

Namespace is the macro/undo-stack class, has no trust decision of its own, and already calls hasOwnProperty on current (and has() checks both maps), so it reads as a separate, already-guarded concern from the settings bug.

set() only records the previous value so the group can restore it; the value the caller asked to define is what gets written, so this reads as undo bookkeeping rather than a lookup that needs an own-property check.

cli.js is a Node convenience binary outside src/, reached only through the katex bin, and prototype pollution in a short-lived CLI process looks unreachable; the advisory describes the library rendering path.

auto-render is a separate contrib package entry that only decides which macros and delimiters apply, not trust itself, so it reads as a neighbouring convenience feature outside the advisory's settings path.

trust and strict are already accepted as functions (and strict as 'warn'/'ignore'/'error'), and an explicitly undefined own value already falls back to the default, so an own-property read is assumed to be value-agnostic and safe to bolt on.

masking: T4 masks T5: while get() still falls through to this.builtins[name] (src/Namespace.ts:85) an inherited macro name already resolves, so the undo capture at src/Namespace.ts:114 makes no visible difference; once get() is own-property-only, set()/endGroup is the remaining way an inherited name becomes an own definition in this.current.

T1 masks T2 in the reported shape: with Object.prototype.trust polluted, the report's new Settings() example is decided at src/Settings.ts:342 and the schema-default read at src/Settings.ts:329 gives no distinguishable result; T2 only shows when the polluted key is default or processor and the options carry no own value.

T1/T2 mask T3 for trust:true callers: when trust is polluted to true every command is allowed anyway, so the forged protocol only matters in the function-valued trust configuration the docs describe (docs/options.md:62-70).

conflicts.what: The natural way to make the options read own-property-only (validate against the schema type or coerce with Boolean(optionValue)) is exactly what destroys the documented function-valued trust/strict forms and the own-undefined fallback that src/Settings.ts:343 currently provides, so the fix for T1 must stay value-agnostic.

The natural fix for T4 (replace or copy the caller's macro map with a null-prototype object so inherited names cannot resolve) breaks the behaviour T5's undo machinery exists to provide: rendering writes \def/\gdef definitions back into the caller's own macros object (docs/options.md:18-25, test/katex-spec.ts:3971-3989), which requires this.current to stay the caller's object (src/Namespace.ts:24).

fairness_risks: trust may be a function and is invoked as this.trust(context) (src/Settings.ts:472-475; docs/options.md:62-70; test/katex-spec.ts:3407-3437): a rule requiring a boolean trust, or coercing with Boolean(), turns a documented allowlist function into unconditional trust.
strict may be a function or 'warn'/'ignore'/'error' (src/Settings.ts:261-267; test/katex-spec.ts:4594-4608): the same coercion or type validation breaks it.

An own property explicitly set to undefined must still fall back to the schema default (src/Settings.ts:343); replacing the '!== undefined' test with hasOwnProperty alone changes throwOnError and maxExpand defaults (the latter removes the expansion limit).

options may legitimately be another Settings instance (test/helpers.ts:79 passes a Settings into katex.__renderToDomTree; test/katex-spec.ts:4590 constructs new Settings(nonstrictSettings)), so a fix that requires a plain object or rejects non-literal options breaks the existing harness.

The macros object is documented as mutated and shared between render calls (docs/options.md:18-25, docs/options.md:72-88; src/Namespace.ts:22-27), and macro values may be functions (docs/options.md:23): a Namespace rewrite that copies/freezes the map or type-checks values breaks globalGroup and function macros.

\htmlClass/\htmlId/\htmlStyle/\htmlData contexts carry no url or protocol (src/functions/html.ts:30-86; docs/options.md:58-60) and existing tests distinguish 'protocol' in context (test/katex-spec.ts:3421-3437), so a T3 fix that always injects a derived protocol changes the documented context shape.
auto-render's other defaults - delimiters, ignoredTags, ignoredClasses, errorCallback (contrib/auto-render/auto-render.ts:135-155) - must keep working if the macros line at 159 is hardened.

An options object whose prototype carries defaults (Object.create({...})) currently works because src/Settings.ts:342 reads through the chain; an own-property rule silently refuses that shape. It is not documented, so refusing it is low risk, but it is a shape a legitimate caller could be using.

design.why: T1+T8 are one edit site with two distinct failure modes (leave the inherited options read, or over-harden and break function-valued trust/strict and the own-undefined fallback), so they are the anchor. T2 forces the solver off the options object onto the schema entries the constructor consumes (schema.default and schema.processor), with the strong dismissal that SETTINGS_SCHEMA is a file-local constant. T3 moves the decision point itself: isTrusted's protocol derivation is bypassed by an inherited protocol, and it looks like the check rather than a site needing a change. T4 moves to the macro namespace in another file where hasOwnProperty is already visible, which is the strongest reason to dismiss. T7 moves to a second package entry (contrib/auto-render) so a solver who reads and edits only src/Settings.ts fails even with a perfect settings fix. Five independent groups across three source files and two package entries, with deepseek-type traps (T2, T4, T7: weak/absent protection behind a plausible dismissal) and a mimo-type trap (T8: the coupled function/undefined value semantics). T5 is a real sixth group but is masked behind T4 and sits in the same Namespace patch, so it adds little; T6 (cli.js) is real but cannot be exercised by the jest harness without a dist build (cli.js:11 requires the built package, package.json:5, and testMatch is **/test/*-spec.ts at package.json:183-185), so it is recorded but not recommended for hidden tests.
